draft.explanation: Starting with $250,000 at a monthly rate of 0.55% (6.6% annual nominal compound monthly), the portfolio grows over 180 months while incorporating scheduled cash flows ($1,500/month for months 1-90, a $50,000 withdrawal at month 60, and $2,000/month for months 91-180). The projected month-180 balance is $1,091,704.30. Against the education funding target of $1,200,000, there is a shortfall of $108,295.70. To cover this shortfall over 180 months, an additional fixed end-of-month contribution of $353.7089 per month is required, which rounds upward to $353.71 per month.

revision.explanation: Re-evaluating the scenario with full mathematical precision: Starting with $250,000 at a monthly interest rate of 0.55%, the initial portfolio grows to $670,977.21 at month 180. Contributions of $1,500/month for months 1–90 accumulate to $285,175.88 at month 180. Contributions of $2,000/month for months 91–180 accumulate to $232,095.99. The $50,000 withdrawal at month 60 compounds to $96,565.38 by month 180. Combining these gives a projected month-180 balance of $1,091,683.70. Compared to the $1,200,000 education funding target, the shortfall is $108,316.30. Covering this shortfall via 180 equal end-of-month payments requires an unrounded extra contribution of approximately $353.7838 per month, which rounds upward to $353.79 per month. The reviewer's proposed balance of $1,111,702.79 is incorrect under the scenario's specified cash flows and interest rate.
